Yang Qiaoli v. Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of Preemptive Right

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Article 230 of the Contract Law, when a lessor sells a leased house, the lessee's preemptive right to purchase under the same conditions shall refer to the right to purchase the house leased by the lessee, not other houses sold by the lessor.

Plaintiff: Yang Qiaoli, female, 35 years old, residing in Chengguan Town, Xingyang City, Henan Province.

Defendant: Henan Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at Suohe Road, Xingyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Haichao, Chairman of the Company.

The plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, filed a lawsuit with the Xingyang People's Court of Henan Province against the defendant, Henan Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd.), for a dispute over infringement of a preemptive right.

The plaintiff alleged: Since June 1995, the plaintiff had been renting a shop unit from the defendant to operate a photography business, with the lease contract expiring on December 30, 2002. During the lease period, the plaintiff received a notice from the defendant stating that the house had been sold to others and asked the plaintiff to negotiate lease matters with the new property owner. This act of the defendant deprived the plaintiff of her preemptive right. The plaintiff requested the court to revoke the defendant's sale of the house and confirm that the plaintiff had a preemptive right to purchase the house.

The plaintiff submitted the following evidence:

1. A notice dated June 22, 2002, bearing the seal of Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., to prove the infringement.
2. A lease agreement signed on June 1, 2001, and three rent receipts dated December 25, 2001, April 5, 2002, and July 22, 2002, to prove the lease of the house and that the lease period covered the entire year of 2002.
3. Testimonies of witnesses Xu Weidong, Shen Qingmei, and Feng Weilin, to prove that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had sold a total of 12 units (24 shop units) including the house rented by Yang Qiaoli, as a whole, in late May or early June 2002, at a price of RMB 1.58 million; and that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had posted a notice of the above sale on the pillars at the entrance of its premises.

The defendant argued: Although the defendant had sold some houses, the house rented by the plaintiff had not been sold, and the defendant had never notified the plaintiff of any change in property rights. The plaintiff and the defendant still maintained a normal lease relationship. The plaintiff's claims were untrue and should be dismissed.

The defendant submitted the following evidence:

1. A copy of the rent receipt stub dated July 22, 2002, stating: "Received from Yang Qiaoli Photography Studio the rent for July-September 2002, in the amount of RMB 2,400." This was used to prove that even after the plaintiff filed the lawsuit, the lease relationship still existed, and the house rented by Yang Qiaoli had not been sold.
2. A shop sale agreement dated June 1, 2002, and a receipt dated May 29, 2002, stating: "Received from Zhang Wenxue the purchase price for the 11 first-floor shop units of the two residential buildings at the east gate of the factory, totaling RMB 1.38 million." This was used to prove that the houses sold by Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. to Zhang Wenxue did not include the house rented by Yang Qiaoli.

The court presided over the cross-examination and authentication of evidence by both parties. The defendant, Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., argued: The evidence 1 submitted by the plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, was authentic, but the 'overall sale' mentioned in the notice did not include the house rented by Yang Qiaoli, and the notice did not bear the name of the addressee, so it could not be proved that it was served on Yang Qiaoli; evidence 2 was also authentic, but the lease agreement only proved the existence of an indefinite lease relationship between the parties, not that the lease period covered the entire year of 2002; the testimonies of the witnesses in evidence 3 were inconsistent with the facts. The actual content of the notice posted was: "Upon resolution of the board of directors, the 12 first-floor shop units on the east side of the building, with the second unit from the west to east reserved for the company's water pump accessories sales department and not for sale, the other 11 units are to be sold as a whole at a price of RMB 1.38 million. Interested bidders, please register at the company office. The successful bidder will be determined by the order of payment." The notice was posted on May 28, 2002, and was torn down on the afternoon of May 29 because someone had paid to purchase.

The plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, argued: The evidence 1 submitted by the defendant, Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., was authentic, but it could not prove that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had not sold the house rented by Yang Qiaoli; the content of evidence 2 was contradictory and forged, and should not be admitted.

The Xingyang People's Court found the following facts:

Since June 1995, the plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, had been renting a house from the defendant, Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., to operate a photography business. Article 4 of the lease agreement signed by Yang Qiaoli and Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. on June 1, 2001, stipulated: "The lessee must renew the lease contract for the following year with the lessor before December 25 of the current year and pay the full rent for half a year or one year in a lump sum. Payment must be made before use." On December 25, 2001, and April 5, 2002, Yang Qiaoli paid rent to Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. On June 22, 2002, Ma Rulong, an employee of Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. responsible for water, electricity, and rent, delivered to Yang Qiaoli a notice from Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., which stated: "Since the company's shop units have been sold as a whole to others and the property rights have changed, the lease agreement originally signed with you by our company expired on June 30, 2002. Upon receipt of this notice, please negotiate specific lease matters with the current buyer. This notice is hereby given." Yang Qiaoli believed that the matters in this notice infringed upon her preemptive right and therefore filed this lawsuit. After filing the lawsuit, Yang Qiaoli paid rent to Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. on July 22, 2002, and Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. issued a rent receipt to Yang Qiaoli.

The Xingyang People's Court held:

Article 230 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "When a lessor sells a leased house, it shall notify the lessee within a reasonable time, and the lessee shall have the right of preemptive purchase under the same conditions." Article 118 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC (For Trial Implementation) provides: "When a lessor sells a leased house, it shall notify the lessee three months in advance. The lessee shall have the right of preemptive purchase under the same conditions; if the lessor sells the house in violation of this provision, the lessee may request the people's court to declare the sale invalid." According to the above provisions, for a lessee to exercise the right of preemptive purchase, the following conditions must be met: 1. There must be a legally valid lease contract between the lessee and the lessor. If the lease contract is not established, is invalid, is revoked, or is terminated due to expiry of the term, the lessee does not enjoy this right. 2. The right of preemptive purchase can only be enjoyed after the lessor decides to sell the leased house, and must be exercised within three months of receiving the sale notice. 3. The lessee must have the right of preemptive purchase under the same conditions. The term 'same conditions' mainly refers to the price and the time and method of payment. If the third party's offer conditions are better than the lessee's, the lessee does not have the right of preemptive purchase. From the lessor's perspective, if it sells the leased house without notifying the lessee, or sells the house without seeking the lessee's opinion within the valid period of the notice, or does not sell the leased house to the lessee when the lessee and the third party offer the same price, these are all illegal acts infringing the lessee's right of preemptive purchase.

The lease agreement signed by the plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, and the defendant, Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., represented true intentions, complied with legal provisions, had been performed for many years, and was a valid contract. When the lessor sold the house leased by Yang Qiaoli, Yang Qiaoli had the right of preemptive purchase.

Article 64, Paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "A party has the responsibility to provide evidence in support of its own claims." Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures provides: "A party has the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which its claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based." "If there is no evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove the party's factual claims, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear adverse consequences." Since the plaintiff, Yang Qiaoli, claimed that her right of preemptive purchase was infringed, she had the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the existence of the infringing facts. The facts to be proved include: 1. There was a legally valid lease relationship between the parties; 2. The lessor decided to sell or had already sold the leased house without notifying the lessee, or although notified, sold the leased house to a third party before the valid period of the notice expired, or sold the leased house to a third party when the lessee and the third party offered the same price. Looking at the evidence submitted by Yang Qiaoli, it could only prove that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had sold some houses, but could not prove that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. decided to sell or had already sold the house leased by Yang Qiaoli. Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. also did not admit Yang Qiaoli's claims. Moreover, after filing the lawsuit, Yang Qiaoli paid rent to Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., and Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. accepted the rent. This fact proved that the house lease relationship between the parties still existed. Therefore, Yang Qiaoli's lawsuit based on the infringement of her preemptive right lacked factual evidence, and her request was not supported.

Accordingly, the Xingyang People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 7, 2002:

Reject the plaintiff Yang Qiaoli's claim.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by the plaintiff Yang Qiaoli.

Yang Qiaoli, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: The facts that the appellee Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. sold the leased house to others during the lease term and deprived the lessee of her preemptive right are evident. The appellee not only sold the leased house but also received the purchase price, and the evidence claiming the house had not been sold was forged. The appellant requested the court to set aside the original judgment and modify it to support the appellant's claims.

Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. argued: The appellant claimed that the property rights of her leased house had changed, but could not produce conclusive evidence to support her claim, so her claim should not be supported. The first-instance judgment was correct and should be upheld.

The Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court, upon hearing the case, confirmed the facts found in the first instance and additionally found: The house transferred by the appellee Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. to Zhang Wenxue had not yet undergone property registration for transfer; Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had mortgaged its other houses (including the house leased by the appellant Yang Qiaoli) to a bank and had registered the mortgage with the property department.

The Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court held:

Article 63 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures provides: "The people's court shall make a judgment based on the facts of the case that can be proved by evidence." Article 64 provides: "Judicial personnel shall, in accordance with legal procedures, examine evidence comprehensively and objectively, independently judge the admissibility and probative value of evidence based on legal provisions, judicial ethics, logical reasoning, and daily life experience, and disclose the reasons and results of such judgment." The preemptive right provided by law means that when a lessor sells a leased house, the lessee may purchase the house leased by the lessee under the same conditions; the lessee does not have a preemptive right for other houses sold by the lessor. The evidence submitted by the appellant Yang Qiaoli could only prove that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had sold some houses and received the purchase price, but could not prove that the house leased by her had been sold by Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. As long as Yang Qiaoli could not prove that the house she leased had been sold by Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd., she could not claim a preemptive right based on the fact that Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. had sold other houses. The sale of other houses by Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. was irrelevant to Yang Qiaoli. The second instance found that the disputed house had been mortgaged by Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. to a bank, further proving that the property owner of the house was still Zhongzhou Pump Industry Co., Ltd. and that the ownership of the house had not transferred. Yang Qiaoli's grounds of appeal lacked factual basis and could not be established, so her appeal request was not supported. The first instance, having conducted a comprehensive and objective examination of the evidence in this case in accordance with legal procedures, found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be upheld.

Accordingly, the Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on March 14, 2003:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 100 shall be borne by the appellant Yang Qiaoli.
